Definition: perhaps from G260; sand (as heaped on the beach):--sand.
BiblicalUsage: Sand, as heaped on the beach, and Jesus and Paul use it for the two ends of counting. Every one that heareth these sayings of mine, and doeth them not, shall be likened unto a foolish man, which built his house upon the sand. And Isaiah cries concerning Israel, Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, a remnant shall be saved; the word is the sand that cannot be numbered and the sand that cannot hold a house.
TheologicalSignificance: A word for sand carries no doctrine of its own; its weight is the two pictures, that the sand is too many to count and too weak to build on.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
